Four of the Titans' final five games are at Cbus Super Stadium so they get a great opportunity to build momentum for next year and give their loyal fans renewed hope of a first finals berth since 2021.

NRL Casualty Ward: Surgery for McLean; Munster, Murray return
Panthers centre Casey McLean has had surgery on a fractured hand but is expected to miss only 1-2 matches.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The injury to McLean sees three-time premiership winner Izack Tago promoted to the starting side for Friday night's bumper clash with the Warriors, who have named gun fullback Taine Tuaupiki on the bench as he looks to return from a foot injury.
In Friday night's other monster showdown, the Roosters have winger Billy Smith back from illness and prop Lindsay Collins set for his first game since Round 17 after ongoing concussion issues, while the Bulldogs get star back-rower Sitili Tupouniua back from a hamstring injury.
Huge ins at South Sydney as well where skipper Cameron Murray (calf) plays his first game since Round 20 while Tallis Duncan (hamstring) and David Fifita (suspension) are also back to face the Eels.
The Storm receive a boost with five-eighth Cameron Munster returning after four games out following surgery for knee cartilage damage. Centre Jack Howarth (shoulder) also returns but Jahrome Hughes remains sidelined with a hamstring injury.

items.snippet: Tips: Joey expects ‘dead cat bounce’ from under-siege Cowboys    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Andrew Johns is adamant that the Cowboys will rebound from their humiliating 70-point defeat to the Roosters with a “dead cat bounce” win over the Titans in Thursday night’s Queensland derby .
Todd Payten’s team has fallen out of the eight after their dismal last start 82-12 loss at home and face a battle to claw their way to finals in the last five rounds of the regular season.
Scott Drinkwater after the Cowboys were thumped by the Roosters in round 22. Getty Images
A win over the 14th placed Titans will be viewed as crucial to their chances of booking a spot in the playoffs, with the in form Bulldogs leaping them into eighth spot due to the scale of the Cowboys’ defeat, which ravaged their for and against.
The Cowboys are level on 26 competition points with both the Rabbitohs (seventh) and Bulldogs (eighth) and have a bye up their sleeve, but a loss on Thursday night would be a serious blow due to their shocking -98 points difference.
With injuries to inspirational halfback and captain Tom Dearden and Origin back-rower Jeremiah Nanai, the Cowboys have their backs against the wall. Only two teams in premiership history have bounced back from 70-point plus defeats to win the following week - the Sharks in 2003 and Canterbury in 1935 - but Johns expects them to “scrap and fight for everything” for a morale-boosting turnaround.
“There’s an expression in the stockbroking world: dead cat bounce. So when it plummets, bounce,” Johns told Wide World of Sports’ NRL Tips , referring to the expression that applies to public companies whose share price go into freefall then have a slight recovery. The grim term comes from the Wall Street saying that “even a dead cat will bounce if it falls from a great height”.
“We’re going to know what’s under the bonnet for the Cowboys,” Johns added.
